state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Why do you think Fido falling asleep would cause the graph to have a negative slope? Can you think of any other reasons why the graph might show a decrease in distance from the home?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, I guess if he was asleep the line would just be flat, wouldn't it? So maybe... does the negative slope mean he's moving backwards? Like walking back towards his home? But I'm confused because I thought negative always meant something bad was happening.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Why do you think negative always means something bad? Can you think of any situations where negative values can actually be positive or neutral?

score.justification_pass1: While the student successfully self-corrects the core misconception about rest vs. movement (recognizing flat means stationary), the teacher's final turn diverts attention to an irrelevant tangent about negative numbers rather than consolidating understanding of the distance-time graph interpretation.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses probing questions to guide the student's thinking, never provides direct answers, and effectively uses the student's misconception about 'negative always means something bad' as a counterexample opportunity to expose flawed reasoning.
